description: A compute that fails is never cached (#lzasyncerrfixture). The caller whose read triggered the failing run receives that run's error; the next read re-runs the body. On the async plane this is the `Error → Computing` transition (docs/async.md § Async slot state machine, LazilyFormal.AsyncSlotState `SlotEvent.retry`): a slot in `Error` holds no cached result. On the synchronous plane it is the same contract with no state to name — a throwing compute leaves nothing behind to serve. A binding that stores the error and replays it to every later reader makes a transient failure (a timed-out fetch, a disconnected peer, a momentary OOM) permanent for the lifetime of the node, with no read path able to recover it. Every assertion here is on `computes_of`, not on the error: a caching binding also raises on every read, it just runs the body once — so an error-only assertion passes against both behaviors and is exactly how lazily-go, lazily-dart and lazily-zig stayed divergent from lazily-rs, lazily-py, lazily-js, lazily-kt, lazily-cs and lazily-cpp under green suites. `fail_next` arms the next N computes of a node to raise; it creates nothing and does not change the node's dependency set, so the recovering run re-registers the same edges. The fixture opens with a baseline read so the counter starts from the same place on a context that materializes at creation and one that materializes on first read. An armed failure needs an invalidation to force the recompute it fails, so this fixture assumes a demand-driven (lazy) recompute: a context that recomputes eagerly at write time consumes the arming during `set_cell` rather than during the read, which is a scheduling difference rather than a caching one and belongs in that binding's per-model skip ledger, not in a loosened assertion here.

expect.note: baseline: one compute, whether the context materialized at creation or on this read
a cached success is served without re-running — this is what makes the counters below discriminating
the invalidated read runs the armed body and that run raises
THE CONTRACT: the next read re-runs rather than replaying the stored error, so the node recovers to the value its current dependencies imply. A caching binding raises here and reports computes_of 2
and the recovered value caches normally — recovery does not leave the node permanently hot
a persistently failing node re-runs on every read: one compute per read, not one compute total
second consecutive failure — a caching binding is still at 4 here while raising the same error
recovery after repeated failure, against the dependency value written while the node was failing — the failing runs did not drop the edge
the recovered node still tracks `src`: the failing runs re-registered their dependencies rather than leaving the node detached
